one_liner: Research CUDA SpGEMM on 16x16 sparse tiles; PPoPP '22 reports wins over cuSPARSE on 139 of 142 large matrices.
what_it_does: Computes C = A*B on NVIDIA GPUs (double precision by default) with every operand stored as a grid of 16x16 tiles, keeping only non-empty tiles, each as a small CSR. The repo is a benchmark program, not a library: './test -d 0 -aat 0|1 A.mtx' reads one Matrix Market file, overwrites its values with i % 10, converts it to tiles on the host, computes A*A (square A only) or A*A^T, prints step timings and GFLOPS, appends CSV rows under ../data/, and optionally checks against cuSPARSE. For general A*B you would call the host function tilespgemm(SMatrix*, SMatrix*, SMatrix*, ...) yourself after csr2tile conversion; C comes back in the tiled format, not CSR.
how_it_is_fast: Tiling turns SpGEMM into three bounded steps. Step 1 finds which C tiles are non-empty with a tile-level SpGEMM using a sparse accumulator. Step 2 computes each C tile's nonzero pattern with bitwise ORs of 16-bit row masks, so C is allocated exactly, with no intermediate-product buffers. Step 3 computes values: it intersects A's tile row with B's tile column by binary search (positions from step 2 are cached speculatively), bins C tiles by nonzero count (thresholds 32/224/256) and picks a sparse or dense accumulator in shared memory per bin. The paper's argument is that this fixes load imbalance, intermediate-buffer sizing and accumulator design at once.
when_to_use: Benchmarking or researching GPU SpGEMM on large square matrices (the paper uses at least one billion flops each) for C = A^2 or C = A*A^T, where it beat cuSPARSE's generic SpGEMM on 139 of 142 matrices.
Matrices whose nonzeros cluster into dense-ish 16x16 blocks (FEM, structural, banded), where per-tile bitmask symbolic work and dense on-chip accumulators pay off.
Pipelines that can keep matrices in a tiled format end to end, so the host-side CSR-to-tile conversion and tile-to-CSR conversion of C (both outside the reported SpGEMM time) are amortized.
Ampere-class NVIDIA GPUs like the paper's RTX 3090 and RTX 3060 (the Makefile targets sm_86).
when_not_to_use: Any reuse in a product: the repo has no LICENSE and the README names none, so the code is not clearly reusable; spECK and OpSparse are MIT.

Very large inputs or recent toolchains: open issue #6 (2025) reports a NULL-pointer error and a segfault on HV15R (283M nonzeros) and a 97.5M-nonzero matrix on an RTX 4090 with CUDA 11.8; open issue #5 (2024) reports a build error under CUDA 12.2; open issue #4 (2023) reports '__builtin_ia32_rndscaless_round is undefined' at build time. None shows a reply.

Hypersparse or irregular matrices where spECK's per-row hashing wins: spECK was faster on 48 of the 142 paper matrices, and a later third-party study (snippet only) puts TileSpGEMM's average speedup over cuSPARSE at 3.47x, below spECK (5.67x) and OpSparse (4.91x).
Code that needs a CSR-in, CSR-out API, single precision out of the box, 64-bit indices (m, n and nnz are int) or non-x86 hosts.
Anything needing maintenance: last commit 2022-11-09, 5 open issues and an open undefined-behavior PR, all without maintainer response.

integration.form: source-drop (single nvcc compile of src/main.cu with header-only .h files; no library target)
integration.dependencies: CUDA runtime and cuSPARSE (cuSPARSE only for the reference check), OpenMP on the host; src/ vendors its own copies of cuda_fp16.h and cuda_fp16.hpp
integration.min_toolchain: CUDA 11.x (Makefile hard-codes /usr/local/cuda-11.4); tested on Ubuntu 18.04/20.04 per README; CUDA 12.2 build failure reported (issue #5)
integration.platforms: NVIDIA GPUs (Makefile builds compute_61 PTX to sm_86 only; compute capability 8.6 recommended); x86-64 Linux host (common.h includes x86intrin.h and immintrin.h, and the build passes -mfma)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the host function tilespgemm() does its own cudaMalloc calls for every operand and for C
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — inputs must be converted from CSR into its SMatrix tile structure, C is returned in tiles, and the shipped driver only squares A or forms A*A^T

gotchas: The reported SpGEMM time (gettimeofday, one run since REPEAT_NUM is 1, no warm-up) covers the three GPU steps plus allocations of C, but not CSR-to-tile conversion of A and B, which the paper reports separately, nor tile-to-CSR conversion of C.

main.cu replaces the input matrix values with i % 10 before multiplying, so the driver's results are not your matrix's product; CHECK_RESULT defaults to 1 in common.h, which adds a host-side tile2csr and a cuSPARSE run.

Open PR #2 (2022-10-14) reported an out-of-bounds read and wrong-size memsets in csr2tile.h (reproduced on RTX 3090, RTX 2080 and GTX 1650 Ti) and a use-after-free in main.cu under CHECK_RESULT. After the November 2022 re-upload of src/, the PR's remaining diff is 2 added lines and 1 removed line in main.cu, so the use-after-free fix is probably still unmerged; the csr2tile.h memsets now look size-correct, but the out-of-bounds fix was not confirmed.

Issue #3: on a GTX 1650 Ti the cuSPARSE reference returned nnzC = 0 for cant and pdb1HYS, so the built-in check prints 'cuSPARSE failed!' even when TileSpGEMM's count is right; do not rely on the harness alone for validation.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick spECK (MIT, CSR in and out, float and double) or OpSparse (MIT, higher average speedup over cuSPARSE in the third-party snippet) for anything you ship. TileSpGEMM is worth studying when your matrices are block-structured and you can stay in its tiled format, or as the reference for the tile approach next to the same lab's TileSpMV and DASP.
verified_claims_summary: Per the PPoPP '22 abstract (search snippets; paper blocked here), on GeForce RTX 3090 and RTX 3060 over 142 square SuiteSparse matrices of at least one billion flops each (C = A^2 and C = A*A^T), TileSpGEMM beat cuSPARSE, bhSPARSE, NSPARSE and spECK on 139, 138, 127 and 94 matrices, with maxima of 2.78x, 145.35x, 97.86x and 3.70x. The repo's cuSPARSE baseline is the generic cusparseSpGEMM API (workEstimation/compute/copy) built with nvcc -O3 against CUDA 11.4; averages, CPU model and cuSPARSE version were not seen.
status_note: Abandoned since 2022-11-09, with no license (reference only) and unanswered crash and build reports.
